s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic, progressive, asymptomatic, arc-shaped, depressed skin lesion with localized hair loss on the scalp and forehead
salient_findings: Arc-shaped, depressed skin groove on the left side of the forehead, frontal scalp, and vertex area
Localized linear hair loss and hair thinning on the left scalp area
Dermoscopic examination revealed short vellus hairs, yellow dots, and honeycomb hyperpigmentation
key_facts: The patient is a man in his 50s
The lesion began approximately 10 years earlier
The patient received 2 doses of intralesional steroid via injection on a small bald patch on the vertex
The lesion gradually progressed to the frontal scalp and eventually made a linear furrow on the left side of his forehead
The patient denied any trauma history
The patient had no history of connective tissue disease
No evidence of systemic involvement, such as arthralgia, photosensitivity, or skin rashes
Dermoscopic examination revealed several short vellus hairs, yellow dots, and honeycomb hyperpigmentation
The result of a hair pull test was negative
Histopathologic examination showed predominant lymphocytic infiltrates in perifollicular and periappendageal regions of the dermis and lobular panniculitis
Direct immunofluorescence was positive with granular deposition of IgG, IgA, IgM, C3, C1q, and fibrinogen in the dermal blood vessels

shortlist.label: lichen planopilaris
shortlist.why_kept: Chronic, progressive, asymptomatic, arc-shaped, depressed skin lesion with localized hair loss on the scalp and forehead, consistent with lichen planopilaris

shortlist.label: frontal fibrosing alopecia
shortlist.why_kept: Linear furrow on the left side of the forehead and localized hair loss on the scalp, consistent with frontal fibrosing alopecia

shortlist.label: discoid lupus erythematosus
shortlist.why_kept: Histopathologic examination showed predominant lymphocytic infiltrates in perifollicular and periappendageal regions of the dermis and lobular panniculitis, consistent with discoid lupus erythematosus

shortlist.label: folliculitis decalvans
shortlist.why_kept: Dermoscopic examination revealed several short vellus hairs, yellow dots, and honeycomb hyperpigmentation, consistent with folliculitis decalvans

shortlist.label: linear scleroderma
shortlist.why_kept: Linear, curved-line, depressed, alopecic patches on the left side of the vertex and frontal scalp area, consistent with linear scleroderma

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of an asymptomatic, arc-shaped, depressed skin groove on the left side of his forehead, frontal scalp, and vertex area, along with localized linear hair loss and hair thinning, is consistent with frontal fibrosing alopecia. The disease's gradual progression over 10 years and the presence of short vellus hairs, yellow dots, and honeycomb hyperpigmentation on dermoscopic examination also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: lichen planopilaris
rejected.why: While lichen planopilaris can cause scarring alopecia, the patient's presentation and histopathologic findings are more consistent with frontal fibrosing alopecia.

rejected.label: discoid lupus erythematosus
rejected.why: The patient had no history of connective tissue disease and no evidence of systemic involvement, making discoid lupus erythematosus less likely.

rejected.label: folliculitis decalvans
rejected.why: Folliculitis decalvans typically presents with inflammatory papules and pustules, which were not observed in this patient.

rejected.label: linear scleroderma
rejected.why: Linear scleroderma can cause skin lesions, but the patient's presentation and histopathologic findings are more consistent with frontal fibrosing alopecia.
